To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
amylopectin fine structure and starch granule architecture is influenced by the composition and organization of protein complexes of enzymes involved in starch synthesis.

the starch phenotype of a maize starch branching enzyme mutant depends on the nature of the mutation, and is determined by the complement of hetero-oligomeric complexes of starch biosynthesis enzymes in the amylopectin granules.

the starches of the two allelic variants of the ae− mutant, ae1.1 and ae1.1, have different properties, which are related to the differences in protein–protein interactions that occur in the amylopectin synthase complexes in their respective amyloplasts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of protein phosphorylation in regulating the organization and assembly in the amyloplatst of the protein complexes that control amylopectin biosynthesis.
the identification of novel protein–protein interaction networks in the amylopectin biosynthetic pathway and their contribution to the formation of starch granules in maize.

the role of SBEIIa and SBEIIb isoforms in starch biosynthesis, and the role that the amylose extensor mutations have in altering the organization of the starch biosynthetic complexes in the amylopectin biosynthetic pathway, and how the resulting changes in protein–protein interactions affect the structure of the starch granules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the starch granule is the result of a complex series of events, including the synthesis, phosphorylation, and assembly of proteins, the synthesis of starch, and the interaction of these proteins with the starch.
the ae− mutations are allelic and that they affect SBEIIb, but that they do not affect its catalytic activity.
the amylopectin structure and starch granule morphology of ae1.1 and ae1. 2 are the result of the loss of a functional SBEIIb and the consequent altered protein interactions in the amylo-plast.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the starches of the ae1 mutants are a consequence of altered protein–protein interactions, and that the nature of the interactions is determined by the nature of the mutation.
the starch granule is a dynamic entity, which is constantly being remodeled by the enzymes of starch biosyntheses.

the amylopectin phenotype in starches of ae− maize is a consequence of the loss of SBEII activity and the resulting changes in protein–protein interactions that affect the assembly and organization of enzymes of starch synthesis in amyloplasts.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the starch phenotype of ae1.1 and ae1. 2 are different and that this difference is related to the presence of the SBEIIa protein in ae1. 1 and its absence in ae1.1, and the presence of the catalytically inactive, phosphorylated form of SBE IIb in ae1,2.

the amylose-extender mutation in maize is allelic, and that the starch phenotype of this mutation is dependent on the specific amino acid sequence of SBEIIa and the nature of the SBEIIa/SBEIIb heterodimers.
